name: Vansen ArcGuard Insulated Shock-Resist Glove
description:
High-voltage insulation gloves used by electrical systems crews, transit infrastructure maintenance, and unlicensed grid tappers alike. Outer shell is matte industrial yellow with black hazard banding at the cuff — sun-faded on most working pairs to a pale mustard. The triple-layer construction sandwiches a dielectric rubber core between abrasion-resistant syn-textile inner and outer layers.

Knuckle and palm zones are thickened for mechanical protection. The extended gauntlet cuff seals with a rolled-bead edge that mates with standard insulated coverall sleeves. A small embossed voltage rating stamp on the wrist reads 40kV — though street-market versions often have the rating faked upward.
functionality: Rated 40kV dielectric insulation (genuine units). Mechanical impact resistance at knuckle and palm. Rolled-bead cuff seals against insulated coverall sleeves. Resists tearing from cable handling and conduit work.
what_it_says: You work inside the city's nervous system and you know exactly how badly it can hurt you.
story_hooks: A maintenance worker is found unconscious near a junction box — their Vansen ArcGuards were genuine, but something punched through the dielectric layer deliberately.
A street vendor is moving counterfeit ArcGuards with faked 80kV stamps; three grid tappers have already been hospitalized and none of them reported it.
A pair of these gloves is the only item recovered from a flooded Tier 1 transformer vault — the worker's name is stenciled inside, but they were declared dead six months ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: Industrial work glove with aggressive safety aesthetics. Extended gauntlet cuff, bulbous padded knuckles, flared wrist opening. High-visibility presence even when faded. Suggests competence, danger exposure, and manual infrastructure work.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, accommodating over standard coverall sleeves. Gauntlet sits mid-forearm with rolled bead edge for seal. Knuckle and palm areas noticeably thickened, creating a blocky silhouette at fingers and heel.
physical_description.primary_material: Triple-layer construction: outer abrasion-resistant syn-textile (matte finish), dielectric rubber core, inner syn-textile. Heavy gauge throughout.
physical_description.texture: Outer shell smooth but dull matte; knuckle/palm zones quilted or embossed for grip and texture definition. Rolled cuff edge creates subtle beading. Gauntlet interior slightly tacky from rubber exposure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte industrial yellow primary with black hazard banding at cuff (chevron or stripe pattern). Most field units sun-faded to pale mustard or cream-yellow. Embossed voltage rating stamp in dark gray/black on wrist.
physical_description.closures: Rolled-bead cuff edge creates friction seal with coverall sleeves; no additional fasteners. Glove opening sized for snug gauntlet fit.
distinctive_features: Embossed 40kV voltage rating stamp on wrist (often tampered with on black-market pairs)
Triple-layer dielectric construction visible at cuff opening
Thickened knuckle caps and reinforced palm zone with visible quilting or embossing
Black hazard banding at cuff transition
Rolled bead edge at gauntlet opening for coverall sleeve seal
Sun-faded or weathered coloration common on street-worn pairs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 (working class) — standard issue for licensed grid maintenance; Tier 5 (sub-grade) when worn by unlicensed grid tappers and salvage crews.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals infrastructure worker, electrician, transit maintenance crew, or underground grid-tapper. Wearing these marks someone as either corpo-adjacent (licensed) or street-level risk-taker (unlicensed). Common across GLMZ electrical sector regardless of legal status.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and faded from field use. Cuffs may be creased or rolled. Black banding dulled. Minor scuffs on knuckles and palms. Voltage ratings on street pairs often hand-amended or re-stamped.
